correctness.rationale: Every nonempty Y retracts by recursively collapsing empty children, and cross-child distance bounds ensure global 1-Lipschitz maps. For a ball with at least two points of Y and a child missing Y, two choices of image of the empty child give distinct retractions, proving necessity. If each child is occupied, compare x and any fixed y in the child: d(r(x),y)<=d(x,y)<diam(B), forcing the image into the same child, so all restrictions are independent and uniqueness reduces by induction to each child. Singleton Y is forced constant. Enumerative product, regular recurrence U_h=q^h+U_(h-1)^q and congruence rank support follow. The normalized log U_h / q^h rises to a positive limit; strict upper bounds come from bottom q-leaf balls with at most q+2 allowed subset patterns (q>=3), or 4-leaf binary balls with 14<16 patterns. Independent enumeration of all concrete subsets of 4-leaf ultrametric and all nonexpansive idempotent maps matched unique-retract criterion. The theorem is finite; no infinite ultrametric claim.

final_claim: For any nonempty finite ultrametric X and nonempty Y, there is exactly one nonexpansive retraction X->Y iff every nonsingleton canonical hierarchy ball B with |Y cap B|>=2 has all immediate children meeting Y. Unique-image rank polynomial obeys P_B(z)=|B|z+product(children P_i(z)); for regular q-ary height h the ranks are all and only 1 mod(q-1), and log-density limit c_q lies strictly between 0 and log 2 with exponentially rare uniqueness.
